title: Azure RBAC: Roles, Scopes and Access

header.html: Manage built-in Azure roles; assign roles at different scopes; interpret access assignments
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1What Azure RBAC is

Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) decides who can do what on which Azure resources. An assignment has three parts:

Part Meaning
Security principal Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity
Role definition What they can do: a set of permitted actions
Scope Where: the level at which the role applies

Old wording Do not confuse Azure roles (control access to Azure resources) with Microsoft Entra roles (control access to Entra directory objects, such as Global Administrator, User Administrator).

2Scope and inheritance

The scope hierarchy, from broad to narrow: management group, subscription, resource group, resource.

Permissions are inherited downward: a role assigned at the subscription applies to every resource group and resource beneath it. Assign at the narrowest scope that works (least privilege).

Exam tip

. A role at a higher scope flows down; you cannot remove an inherited role at a lower scope (only change the assignment where it was made).

3Built-in roles

Role Can do
Owner Everything, including assigning roles
Contributor Create and manage all resources, but not assign roles
Reader View resources only
User Access Administrator Manage user access (assign roles) but not manage resources
Resource-specific roles For example Virtual Machine Contributor, Storage Blob Data Contributor, Network Contributor

A role definition lists Actions (control plane), NotActions (excluded), and DataActions (data plane, such as reading blob data). Custom roles can be created when no built-in role fits.

Exam tip

. "Manage resources but must not assign access" = Contributor. "Assign access but not manage resources" = User Access Administrator. "Everything including access" = Owner.

4Assigning and interpreting access

Task Where
Assign a role Access control (IAM) on a scope, Add role assignment, pick the role, the members and the scope
Who has access here? Access control (IAM) > Role assignments (shows inherited assignments too)
Why does this user have access? Check access shows the user's effective roles and where each comes from
Deny Deny assignments (created by Azure Blueprints or managed apps) override allows

Permissions are additive: a user with several role assignments gets the union of all permissions.

Exam tip

. Azure roles control resources; Microsoft Entra roles control the directory. Global Administrator is not an Azure role.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A developer must create and manage virtual machines in one resource group but must not be able to grant access to others. Which role and scope fit best?

  • AOwner at the subscription
  • BVirtual Machine Contributor at the resource group
  • CReader at the subscription
  • DUser Access Administrator at the management group
Show the answer

Answer: B. A resource-specific contributor role at the narrowest scope follows least privilege.

S2A role is assigned at a subscription. What is the effect on a resource group inside it?

  • AThe role does not apply
  • BThe role applies only to new resource groups
  • CThe role is inherited by the resource group
  • DThe role must be assigned again
Show the answer

Answer: C. Role assignments are inherited by child scopes.

S3Which role can assign roles but cannot manage resources?

  • AContributor
  • BReader
  • CUser Access Administrator
  • DOwner
Show the answer

Answer: C. User Access Administrator manages access, not resources.

S4An administrator wants to see why a user can modify a storage account. Which tool shows the effective roles and their sources?

  • ACheck access in Access control (IAM)
  • BAzure Advisor recommendations for the subscription
  • CResource locks on the storage account
  • DTags on the storage account and its resource group
Show the answer

Answer: A. Check access shows the user's effective permissions and where they come from.

S5A user is a Reader on a subscription and a Contributor on one resource group. What can the user do in that resource group?

  • AOnly read, because the Reader role always wins
  • BNothing, because the narrower assignment is ignored
  • CAssign roles to other users in the resource group
  • DContribute, because permissions are additive
Show the answer

Answer: D. Permissions from several assignments are combined.

S6Which is a Microsoft Entra role, not an Azure role?

  • AContributor
  • BReader
  • CGlobal Administrator
  • DOwner
Show the answer

Answer: C. Global Administrator is an Entra directory role.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the three parts of a role assignment?

Show the answer

Security principal, role definition and scope.

R2What is the scope hierarchy?

Show the answer

Management group, subscription, resource group, resource.

R3What can Contributor not do?

Show the answer

Assign roles.

R4What does Reader allow?

Show the answer

Viewing resources only.

R5Are permissions inherited upward or downward?

Show the answer

Downward.

R6Where do you assign a role?

Show the answer

In Access control (IAM) on the chosen scope.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Assignment principal + role + scope
Scopes management group, subscription, resource group, resource; inherited downward
Roles Owner (all + access), Contributor (resources, no access), Reader, User Access Administrator
Tools IAM blade, role assignments, check access
Not the same Azure roles vs Microsoft Entra roles
